🔍 Iran prepares oil tanker convoy to break US blockade — reports More than a dozen oil tankers off Iran’s Kharg Island are reportedly preparing to set sail toward export destinations. According to TankerTrackers, Iran is making preparations to resume oil exports by openly challenging the US Navy blockade rather than trying to evade it. 🔴 The plan is reportedly to force the route open, making the cost of blocking it too high for the US forces. 🔴 Proponents of the convoy strategy state that if a single bullet hits the hull of an Iranian tanker, the oil facilities and terminals of the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, and Bahrain will immediately become part of the equation. 🔴 Fars News invoked the Shahnameh myth of Fereydoun crossing the Arvand River—refusing to wait for the river guardian's permission and riding straight into the water. This signals a shift from covert evasion to a public display of force. 🔴 For years, Iran has built alternative infrastructure, including the Jask port and storage networks in China, to sustain oil flows. Now, Iran appears ready to bring this hidden capability into the light. By turning a shadow fleet operation into a highly visible tanker convoy, Tehran is calling the CENTCOM's bluff. If the US Navy attempts to enforce its blockade, Iran is explicitly threatening to drag the entire Gulf's energy infrastructure into a massive regional war. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime

To help keep the nation’s food supply steady, USDA gives farmers a financial safety net for things like crop insurance or covering losses when factors like bad weather affect harvest yields, according to NextGov.
